question: A
title: Affordable Housing
explanation: The city wants permission to borrow up to $22 million for affordable housing, such as buying and fixing up run-down property, building or renovating homes, and helping people rent or buy.
if_for: The city can borrow the money. Which projects get it, and when, is decided later.
if_against: The city can't borrow this money, so affordable housing work would need other funding.

question: B
title: School Facilities
explanation: The city wants permission to borrow up to $60 million for public schools: building and fixing school buildings, buying equipment, and improving athletic facilities, including some that also serve community health and recreation.
if_for: The city can borrow the money for school facilities. Which schools get it is decided later.
if_against: The city can't borrow this money, so school building work would need other funding.

question: C
title: Community And Economic Development
explanation: The city wants permission to borrow up to $50 million for neighborhood and economic development: cleaning up blighted property, improving neighborhoods, helping people with housing, and supporting businesses.
if_for: The city can borrow the money and use it for loans and grants as well as direct projects. Which ones get funded is decided later.
if_against: The city can't borrow this money, so this kind of development work would need other funding.

question: D
title: Public Infrastructure
explanation: The city wants permission to borrow up to $148 million for public infrastructure: city buildings, libraries, parks, streets, utilities, technology, and similar improvements.
if_for: The city can borrow the money. Which projects get it is decided later.
if_against: The city can't borrow this money, so infrastructure work would need other funding.

question: E
title: Contract Bidding And Awards
explanation: Right now the city charter says contracts must go to the lowest bidder, sets a way to break ties, and requires certain bonds from contractors. This would take those rules out of the charter.
if_for: Those rules are removed on November 7, 2028, unless the city passes its own rules on the topic sooner. The city could then change how it awards contracts through city laws or regulations, without going back to voters.
if_against: The current charter rules on bidding stay in place.

question: F
title: Budget Process And Board Of Estimates
explanation: This changes how the city passes laws and builds its budget. The mayor, not the Board of Estimates, would prepare the budget, and the Board would lose many of its other duties, which could be handed to other city offices. It would also shorten the time to veto a bill and override a veto, end the preliminary budget hearings, and remove the $1 million limit on the emergency fund.
if_for: The changes start on different dates: December 3, 2026 for most of them, November 7, 2028 for charter sections that are removed (unless the city replaces them sooner), and December 5, 2028 for the new veto and approval rules.
if_against: Nothing changes: the Board of Estimates keeps its current duties, and the current budget and veto rules stay.

question: G
title: Franchises And Minor Privileges
explanation: This updates the rules for how outside parties can use city property. The stormwater system could never be sold or rented out. Space in the city's conduit system could be rented out, but the conduit system itself still couldn't be sold. Minor privileges (small permissions to use part of city property) would be granted by a city agency under a process set by city law, instead of by the Board of Estimates. It also removes outdated language about street railways and trackless trolleys.
if_for: Most changes start December 3, 2026. Removed charter sections go away on November 7, 2028, unless the city replaces them sooner.
if_against: The current charter language stays, including the Board of Estimates' role in granting minor privileges.

question: H
title: Department Of Water And Wastewater
explanation: This creates a new city Department of Water and Wastewater with its own director. Responsibility for the water supply and wastewater systems would move over from the Department of Public Works. It also removes the charter requirement that bureaus within Public Works be created or eliminated by city law.
if_for: The new department takes over on January 1, 2029.
if_against: Water and wastewater stay with the Department of Public Works.

question: I
title: Baltimore Baby Fund
explanation: This creates the Baltimore Baby Fund, a separate pot of city money to help improve the financial stability of families with newborns. The city would have to put money in every year, and the fund can also accept donations and grants.
if_for: The fund is created. Each year the city must add 3 cents for every $100 of taxable property value. The money can only be used for families with newborns, and it can't replace newborn funding already in this year's budget.

question: A
title: Affordable Housing Loan
explanation: The city asked for permission to borrow up to $20 million for affordable housing, such as buying and fixing up property, building or renovating homes, helping people rent or buy, and supporting the Affordable Housing Trust Fund.
if_for: The city could borrow the money. Which projects got it was decided later.
if_against: The city couldn't borrow this money through this question. Existing housing programs wouldn't end because of it.

question: B
title: School Loan
explanation: The city asked for permission to borrow up to $55 million for public schools: buying or improving school property, building and rebuilding schools, buying equipment, and improving athletic and other school facilities.
if_for: The city could borrow the money for school projects. Which schools got it was decided later.
if_against: The city couldn't borrow this money through this question. Other school funding wouldn't be affected.

question: C
title: Community And Economic Development Loan
explanation: The city asked for permission to borrow up to $50 million for neighborhood and economic development: redeveloping property, business and job programs, homeownership and home repair help, cultural projects, and tourism.
if_for: The city could borrow the money and use it for loans and grants as well as direct projects. Which ones got funded was decided later.
if_against: The city couldn't borrow this money through this question. Other development programs wouldn't end because of it.

question: D
title: Public Infrastructure
explanation: The city asked for permission to borrow up to $125 million for public infrastructure: streets, bridges, city buildings, libraries, parks, recreation facilities, technology, and trees.
if_for: The city could borrow the money. Which projects got it was decided later.
if_against: The city couldn't borrow this money through this question. Infrastructure work paid for from other sources could still go ahead.

question: E
title: Baltimore City Police Department
explanation: This would write the Police Department into the city charter as a city agency headed by a Police Commissioner. The mayor appoints the commissioner, subject to confirmation, and the commissioner decides how the department is organized and run. The charter would also spell out the department's job (keeping the peace, preventing and investigating crime, enforcing laws, and making arrests) and set the process for creating police districts.
if_for: The department, the commissioner's role and powers, and the officers' duties become part of the charter.
if_against: These provisions aren't added to the charter.

question: F
title: Inner Harbor Park
explanation: This changes a charter rule that dedicates the Inner Harbor shoreline to public park use. It would let up to 4.5 acres (up from 3.2) near Conway Street be used for restaurants, businesses, multifamily housing, and parking. Areas used for housing and parking would no longer count as part of the public park.
if_for: The land-use changes are adopted, and the area allowed for these uses grows from 3.2 to 4.5 acres. Approval alone didn't mean anything was built.
if_against: The current charter restriction stays in place.

question: G
title: Community Reinvestment And Reparations Fund
explanation: This would create a city fund to pay for the work of the Community Reinvestment and Reparations Commission. Money in it would carry over from year to year instead of expiring, and it could only be used for the commission's work, within limits set by state law.
if_for: The fund exists, and the City Council can pass laws on how it is overseen and run. The question doesn't set a dollar amount.

question: H
title: Reducing The Size Of The City Council
explanation: This would shrink the City Council from 14 districts to 8. If it passed, the mayor would have to draw a new district map based on the latest census and give it to the Council by February 1 of the first municipal election year afterward.
if_for: The Council goes down to 8 districts, and the mayor draws new districts.
